name: Vein of Galen Malformation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No standardized formal criteria; diagnosis based on imaging and clinical presentation

criteria.description: Identification of arteriovenous malformation involving the median prosencephalic vein (precursor to the vein of Galen) on MRI or angiography
Presence of congestive heart failure or high-output cardiac failure in neonate or infant
Evidence of hydrocephalus or increased intracranial pressure secondary to venous hypertension

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Imaging confirmation of the malformation plus clinical signs of cardiac failure or neurological symptoms
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis primarily relies on neuroimaging modalities such as MRI, MR angiography, or digital subtraction angiography.

laboratory: Elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) indicating heart failure
Possible anemia secondary to high-output cardiac failure
imaging: MRI/MR angiography showing dilated median prosencephalic vein and arteriovenous shunting
Digital subtraction angiography confirming arteriovenous malformation
Ultrasound with Doppler demonstrating turbulent flow in vein of Galen region
other: Chest X-ray demonstrating cardiomegaly and pulmonary plethora

distinguishingFeatures: Location of fistula outside vein of Galen region

redFlags: Rapidly progressive congestive heart failure in neonate
Signs of increased intracranial pressure (bulging fontanelle, vomiting)
references: Lasjaunias P, et al. Vein of Galen malformations: clinical and radiological aspects. Neurosurg Rev. 2006.
Mullan S, et al. Endovascular treatment of vein of Galen malformations. Neurosurg Clin N Am. 2010.
Orphanet: Vein of Galen malformation. Orphanet Report Series. 2021.
